questions.stem: A coin is flipped twice. Using a tree diagram, what is the probability of getting exactly one head?
questions.explanation: The outcomes are HH, HT, TH, TT. Exactly one head: HT and TH. P = P(HT) + P(TH) = 1/4 + 1/4 = 1/2. Each branch is multiplied (AND), then outcomes are added (OR).

questions.stem: The probability of rain on any day is 0.3, independent of other days. What is the probability of rain on both Monday and Tuesday?
questions.explanation: P(rain Mon AND rain Tue) = 0.3 × 0.3 = 0.09. For independent events, multiply the probabilities along the branches. Option (a) adds instead of multiplying, which is the most common tree diagram error.

A bag has 4 red and 6 blue balls. Two balls are drawn WITH replacement. What is the probability that both are the same colour?
questions.explanation: P(both red) = 4/10 × 4/10 = 16/100. P(both blue) = 6/10 × 6/10 = 36/100. P(same colour) = 16/100 + 36/100 = 52/100 = 13/25. With replacement, probabilities stay the same for the second draw.

questions.stem: Sarah passes her driving test with probability 0.7 on each attempt, independently. She takes the test up to 3 times, stopping when she passes. What is the probability she passes on her third attempt?
questions.explanation: She must fail twice then pass: P = 0.3 × 0.3 × 0.7 = 0.063. She can only reach attempt 3 if she failed the first two. Option (b) ignores the previous failures. Option (c) calculates 0.3³.
